title: Semicon Series 3 | Inside TSMC's "Baipu Plan" and the Hidden Agenda That Revealed It
gist: A short teaser reveals TSMC's previously undisclosed 'Baipu Plan' — a dedicated CoWoS validation line in Kaohsiung where advanced-packaging suppliers will develop and test next-gen technology alongside TSMC, aimed at cutting feedback cycles from weeks to hours as Nvidia and Google push annual AI accelerator refreshes.

themes.theme: TSMC's Baipu Plan for the CoWoS supply chain

insights.claim: TSMC is planning to build a dedicated CoWoS validation line in northern Kaohsiung, not for mass production but for equipment and materials suppliers to jointly develop and test next-generation advanced-packaging technology alongside TSMC.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A dedicated pre-production validation line for the CoWoS supply chain could tighten TSMC's grip on advanced packaging by pulling suppliers deeper into its ecosystem; worth watching for confirmation and named supplier participants.
insights.locator: TSMC plans to build a dedicated CoWoS

insights.claim: The stated goal of TSMC's 'Baipu Plan' is to cut supplier feedback cycles for advanced packaging from weeks to hours by having equipment and materials suppliers develop and test alongside TSMC rather than iterating independently.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Compressing supplier iteration cycles by orders of magnitude, if achieved, would meaningfully shorten CoWoS capacity ramp times industry-wide, a leading indicator given packaging is a known AI-chip bottleneck.
insights.quote: What if TSMC could cut supplier feedback cycles from weeks to hours?

insights.claim: The urgency behind the Baipu Plan stems from Nvidia and Google pushing a new generation of AI accelerators roughly every year, a cadence that is outpacing the ability of the advanced-packaging supply chain to keep up as packaging complexity rises.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Annual AI-accelerator refresh cycles from Nvidia and Google are becoming the pacing item packaging supply chains must match, a bottleneck signal for CoWoS-dependent capacity planning.
insights.locator: Nvidia and Google are pushing toward

insights.claim: TSMC's Baipu Plan reframes supplier relationships from independent, competing iteration into a coordinated team effort across the entire advanced-packaging supply chain.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A shift toward coordinated supplier ecosystems could raise switching costs for packaging-equipment suppliers and deepen TSMC's structural moat in CoWoS.
insights.quote: TSMC's answer is to stop having suppliers fight alone—and turn the entire advanced packaging supply chain into a team.
